witness_description: Triangle K3 on vertices {0,1,2} with all three edge weights equal to 1; partition S={0} vs V\S={1,2}; minimum-weight crossing edge e=(0,1) (weight 1, tied with (0,2)); the spanning tree {(0,2),(1,2)} has total weight 2 = MST weight, so it is an MST, yet it does not contain e.
refutation_explanation: The claim asserts that for ANY partition, the edge of minimum weight crossing it belongs to EVERY MST, with no distinct-weights or unique-minimum hypothesis. In K3 with unit weights, all three spanning trees ({01,02}, {01,12}, {02,12}) have weight 2 and are all MSTs. Edge (0,1) attains the minimum crossing weight for the cut S={0}, but MST {(0,2),(1,2)} omits it. Hence a minimum-weight crossing edge fails to belong to every MST, refuting the claim as stated. (The correct cut property requires the minimum crossing edge to be unique, or weakens the conclusion to membership in SOME MST.)
search_space: All connected simple undirected graphs on n in {2,3,4} vertices (every connected edge subset of K_n), every integer weight assignment from {1,2} on the edges, every nonempty proper vertex partition (S fixed to contain vertex 0), every crossing edge attaining the minimum crossing weight, checked for membership in every MST (all MSTs enumerated by brute force over all (n-1)-edge spanning subsets; exact int arithmetic, deterministic iteration order, first witness reported).
